text.en:
Ria's school bus travelled 30 kilometres in one hour. Her uncle's car did 60 kilometres in the same hour.
"Your uncle's car is faster," said the driver. "It covers more distance in the same time."

Speed is the distance travelled in a unit of time. Speed = distance ÷ time. If a bus travels 60 km in 2 hours its speed is 30 km per hour. Units are metres per second (m/s) or kilometres per hour (km/h).
Time is measured using clocks. People once used sundials and water clocks, then pendulum clocks, and now quartz and digital clocks. A pendulum swings with a regular time period.
A body moving at the same speed all the time has uniform speed, while one that speeds up or slows down has non-uniform speed. A speedometer shows speed and an odometer shows distance covered.
Speed is the distance travelled in one unit of time. Speed equals distance divided by time.
A bus that goes 60 kilometres in 2 hours has a speed of 30 kilometres per hour.
Clocks have changed from sundials to pendulum clocks to digital clocks.
A speedometer shows speed. An odometer shows the distance covered.

problem.en: A train travels 180 km in 3 hours. What is its speed?

text.en: Speed equals distance divided by time.
So its speed is 60 kilometres per hour.

prompt.en: A friend says a car that goes 100 km is always faster than one that goes 50 km. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: We must compare the times too.
50 km in 30 minutes is faster than 100 km in 4 hours.

points.en: A speedometer shows speed and an odometer shows distance.
